newsitem.title: USA: NYC MAC sells $121 mln of bonds in retail period.
newsitem.headline: NYC MAC sells $121 mln of bonds in retail period.

text.p: The Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York sold over $121 million of bonds to individual investors during a one-day presale period, an official with the lead underwriter said on Wednesday.

This was substantially higher than an initial estimate of $75 million seen late last night by another official with the firm, JP Morgan Securities Inc, who at the time noted the orders still were being counted.
While none of the maturities were closed, the sale accounts for over one-fifth of the total offering of $543 million, which will be priced for institutional investors later Wednesday.

Asked what was responsible for the strong demand displayed by individual investors, Peter Clarke, a managing director with JP Morgan, replied: "I think the absolute yield levels; the market has moved up in yield rather dramatically from where it was in February, when the last deal was done."
In February, preliminary data showed the Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York got about $58.7 million of retail of retail orders for its $490 million bond sale planned for Wednesday.
